name: Chart Industries, Inc.

profile.description: Chart Industries designed, engineered, and manufactured process technologies and equipment for gas and liquid molecule handling across what it called the Nexus of Clean — clean power, clean water, clean food, and clean industrials. Operating through Cryo Tank Solutions, Heat Transfer Systems, Specialty Products, and Repair Service & Leasing segments, Chart served LNG, hydrogen, carbon capture, data center cooling, and industrial gas markets globally. The company was acquired by Baker Hughes for $210/share in cash ($10.1B), with the merger closing on July 16, 2026. GTLS was delisted from the NYSE following the merger's completion. Chart now operates as an indirect subsidiary of Baker Hughes.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): The 2023 Howden acquisition was transformative, more than doubling Chart's revenue from ~$1.5B to ~$4.3B and creating a full-solution platform spanning cryogenic equipment, compression, and aftermarket services — fundamentally redefining Chart from a niche equipment maker to an integrated industrial technology provider [1]. Chart expanded into data center cooling and carbon capture markets, though Q1 2026 revenue declined 11.7% YoY to $884.8M, demonstrating execution challenges post-integration [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI-powered products shipping or quantified AI-driven cost savings. Chart's differentiation is in metallurgical engineering expertise rather than digital technology [3]. Market Share (2/2): Chart held dominant global positions in cryogenic equipment for LNG, brazed aluminum heat exchangers, vacuum-insulated storage tanks, and small/mid-scale LNG solutions. Baker Hughes' $10.1B acquisition at $210/share validated this technology and market leadership position [2]. Pipeline (1/2): Strong order pipeline in data center cooling and LNG infrastructure, with Q1 2026 ending backlog of $6.28B providing near-term revenue visibility [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Differentiation came from engineering expertise and installed-base knowledge rather than above-industry R&D spending.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Chart's purpose centered on the 'Nexus of Clean' — clean power, clean water, clean food, and clean industrials — connecting process technology to environmental outcomes [4]. The framework is specific and thoughtful, though it hadn't been validated through decades of execution (the clean energy pivot was 5-7 years old). Community Impact (1/2): Chart's Giving Back and Bright Futures programs supported community education initiatives, and the company published ESG reports reflecting its Inspire Insight score of 68 (ALIGNED) across 21 positive attribution categories. Community investment was modest in scale relative to global operations [4]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor culture/values rating of 2.9/5 is well below average. Employee reviews cited 'no effort to retain talent,' 'constant change in strategy,' 'trigger-happy with layoffs,' and leadership communication concerns [3]. CEO Evanko resigned in November 2025 ahead of the Baker Hughes merger. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider purchases. CEO departure and sale to Baker Hughes suggest monetization rather than long-term conviction.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on growth-stock metrics with PEG excluded (unavailable). D/E of 121% reflects Howden acquisition leverage, scoring 0.78 [5]. ROE of -1.5% is negative (at floor, scoring 0.0 at 2x weight), driven by Howden integration costs, heavy amortization, and Q1 2026 margin compression [1]. Revenue growth YoY of -11.7% scores 0.28, reflecting lower volumes across all segments with gross margin contracting 550bps to 28.4% from unfavorable mix, higher labor/material costs, and tariffs [1]. Estimated 5-year revenue CAGR of ~25% (includes Howden acquisition step-up from ~$1.3B in 2021 to ~$4.3B in 2025) scores 1.0 at 2x weight. Forward P/E of 23.1 scores 0.92 [5]. Profit margin of -0.7% is negative (at floor, scoring 0.0) [5]. Weighted sum of 3.98 across 8 weight units yields score of 5. Pre-acquisition liquidity was ample with ~900K shares/day at ~$205 ($184M daily turnover).

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Chart Industries operated in physical-world industrial manufacturing — designing and building cryogenic tanks, heat exchangers, compressors, and LNG processing equipment [1]. These are highly engineered, custom-fabricated physical products requiring metallurgical expertise and specialized manufacturing capabilities that AI structurally cannot displace. AI data center expansion directly increases demand for Chart's cooling solutions and water treatment infrastructure — Chart was an enabler of AI infrastructure, not a target of disruption. The installed base of thousands of cryogenic systems worldwide created aftermarket service revenue that AI cannot substitute. AI Opportunity (1/1): Chart generated meaningful and growing revenue from AI-related infrastructure. Data center cooling solutions and water treatment equipment for hyperscaler AI facilities represented a direct revenue link to AI growth. Q1 2026 orders improved in Heat Transfer including data center demand, and ending backlog extended to $6.28B partly driven by AI infrastructure investment [1].

infinite_game.summary: Chart Industries demonstrated meaningful infinite game elements — the Howden acquisition was a courageous bet to transform from a niche equipment maker into a full-solution clean energy platform, and the Nexus of Clean framework connected engineering capabilities to environmental purpose. However, weak employee trust (Glassdoor 2.9/5), CEO departure, and the completed Baker Hughes acquisition indicate the company's independent infinite game trajectory has ended, subsumed by a larger company's consolidation strategy. The willingness to sell rather than continue building independently reflects finite-game thinking at the board level.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Chart's 'Nexus of Clean' framework — clean power, clean water, clean food, clean industrials — was a genuine cause connecting process technology to environmental sustainability and human welfare [4]. The Howden acquisition demonstrated strategic commitment to this vision by building an integrated platform for the energy transition. However, the cause hadn't been tested through multi-decade consistency, and the completed Baker Hughes acquisition subsumed this distinct purpose within a larger corporate entity [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Under CEO Evanko, Chart executed the highly leveraged Howden acquisition in 2023, taking on $3.7B in debt to fundamentally transform the company during rising interest rates [1]. This was a bold bet prioritizing long-term platform capability over near-term financial comfort. However, the subsequent sale to Baker Hughes for $210/share, while financially prudent for shareholders, represents choosing a payday over continued independent execution — the opposite of infinite-minded leadership's willingness to sacrifice near-term rewards for long-term capability building.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor data revealed a low-trust environment with culture/values rated 2.9/5 and career opportunities at 2.9/5 [3]. Recurring employee themes included 'constant change in strategy and reorganizing,' 'zero loyalty to long-term employees,' 'rampant incompetency within leadership,' and perception that production workers were undervalued relative to sales teams. CEO Evanko's resignation in November 2025 compounded organizational uncertainty during the Baker Hughes acquisition process. This was not a Circle of Safety environment.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): The 2023 Howden acquisition fundamentally transformed Chart from a niche cryogenic equipment maker (~$1.5B revenue) into an integrated clean energy and industrial technology platform (~$4.3B revenue) spanning compression, aftermarket services, and process technology [1]. This was a transformative reinvention driven by the Nexus of Clean vision rather than desperation. The subsequent expansion into data center cooling represented continued strategic evolution within the new platform.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Chart's competitive language emphasized market leadership and technology dominance rather than learning from rivals. The sale to Baker Hughes reflects a board decision to monetize rather than compete independently — effectively conceding that a larger platform was needed to fully capitalize on the clean energy and data center infrastructure opportunity [2]. No evidence of management referencing competitors' strengths as motivation for improvement.

investment_thesis: Chart Industries was a global leader in cryogenic and process technology positioned at the intersection of LNG infrastructure, hydrogen, carbon capture, and AI data center cooling. The Baker Hughes acquisition closed on July 16, 2026 at $210/share ($10.1B), validating Chart's technology portfolio and market position [2]. Pre-acquisition, Chart demonstrated strong order momentum with ending backlog of $6.28B (up from $5.89B at year-end 2025 and $4.85B at year-end 2024), reflecting a TTM book-to-bill of 1.33x driven by data center cooling, LNG infrastructure, and clean energy demand [1]. The 'Nexus of Clean' framework positioned Chart's technologies across four secular growth megatrends (clean power, water, food, industrials). Full-year 2025 revenue was $4.26B (+2.5% YoY) with adjusted operating margin of 20.7%. Inspire Impact Score of 68 (ALIGNED) reflected strong ESG positioning across 21 positive attribution categories.
thesis_continued: The bear case materialized in operational execution: Q1 2026 revenue declined 11.7% YoY to $884.8M with gross margin contracting 550bps to 28.4% from unfavorable product mix, higher labor/material costs, and tariff impacts, resulting in an EPS loss of $0.36 [1]. Full-year 2025 earnings collapsed 93% to just $13.5M on $4.26B revenue as Howden integration costs, heavy amortization, and margin pressure overwhelmed revenue growth. ROE turned negative (-1.5%) and GAAP profit margin was -0.7%, reflecting the continued burden of acquisition leverage (D/E 121%) on a deteriorating revenue trajectory [5]. Employee culture dysfunction (Glassdoor 2.9/5), CEO departure, and frequent layoffs created talent retention risk at a company where engineering expertise was the primary competitive advantage [3]. The acquisition by Baker Hughes provided shareholders a clean exit at $210/share but ended Chart's independent story.
key_catalysts: Baker Hughes acquisition closed July 16, 2026 at $210/share — shareholders received full cash consideration; Chart's technologies now integrated into Baker Hughes' $30B+ energy technology platform with broader distribution and customer access [2]

Pre-acquisition AI data center cooling demand created a structural growth driver, with Q1 2026 ending backlog of $6.28B reflecting strong order momentum from hyperscaler investment in electricity and cooling infrastructure [1]
Record backlog trajectory — from $4.85B (2024 year-end) to $5.89B (2025 year-end) to $6.28B (Q1 2026) — provided multi-year revenue visibility for the combined Baker Hughes-Chart entity
key_risks: Post-acquisition integration within Baker Hughes may dilute Chart's focused Nexus of Clean identity and engineering culture within a larger, more diversified organization — key technical talent may depart

Pre-acquisition Q1 2026 operational deterioration — revenue down 11.7%, gross margin down 550bps, and negative profit margin — indicated structural Howden integration challenges that Baker Hughes inherits [1]

Employee culture dysfunction (Glassdoor 2.9/5) and CEO departure created talent retention risk that persists through the Baker Hughes integration; engineering expertise is the primary competitive asset at risk [3]

backlog.note: Q1 2026 ending backlog of $6.28B (up from $5.89B at 2025 year-end and $4.85B at 2024 year-end). TTM book-to-bill of 1.33x based on 2025 orders of $5.68B against $4.26B revenue. Order acceleration in Heat Transfer from data center cooling and small-scale LNG demand. Funded backlog estimated at 85%. Backlog-to-revenue ratio of 5.9 quarters provides strong multi-year visibility.
